# Vitelotte (01, engineer) — BAD-093

## Brief
Say in refreshCollab what BAD-090 said in runCollabSync: supersession cancels the PAINT, not the TRANSFER.

refreshCollab(pack, {pull:true}) is how a scene ARRIVES in a room, and its pull sits BELOW the `seq !== collab.seq` guard. onSceneSelected/selectPack fires it un-awaited, so any caller that bumps collab.seq in the window between the info read and the pull abandons the arrival pull with no retry and no error — and the superseding refresh passes pull:false, so it fetches nothing. The person who just opened a collab scene sees an empty room for up to the 60s poll. autoPullWrapped is worse: collabAutoPulled makes it once per room per run, so its single pull being superseded means the wrapped room's takes never get a second attempt at all.

Fix both clients. They are separate implementations of one behaviour that must agree, not shared code.

- web/collabweb-model.js: the guard is the `if (seq !== collab.seq || ...) return false;` after the `info` fetch; the pull branch is `if (pull && !collab.offline) { ... }` below it.
- renderer/app.js: the same pair around `window.vc.collabStatus` / `window.vc.collabPull`.

The shape BAD-090 settled on is the reference: runCollabSync in web/collabweb-sync.js guards the transfer on scene identity only ((state.scene && state.scene.id) === sceneId), never on collab.seq, and leaves the seq check for the repaint. Read test/collabreads.test.js's head comment before you write anything — it is the written record of why the read sits where it sits, and its 'a focus poll landing mid-cycle does not cancel the cycle`s pull' test is the identical mechanism for the sync path.

Decide, and write the reason down where the next person will hit it:
- Which conditions still cancel the pull. Scene identity must; collab.seq must not. `collab.offline` and `collabActive()` are read before the pull today — say what they mean once the pull moves above the guard.
- What the superseded call returns and what it must NOT leave behind. A superseded refresh still returns false, and must not toast, must not overwrite collab.remote/collab.resolved, must not repaint or re-arm the poll on top of a newer call's state. The pull's WRITES go to the take store and are wanted whoever asked for them; the paint is the part that belongs to the current call only.
- Whether moving the pull above the guard changes the wire order BAD-090 pinned. It must not: the read stays at the tail of the sync cycle and before the first download-url. If your change moves a read, you have changed BAD-090's invariant and the answer is a different fix, not a relaxed test.

Extend test/collabreads.test.js (do not start a new file): a test per client proving an arrival pull survives a concurrent seq bump — the takes land in the remote store — and a test proving the superseded call still does not paint. Build the broken version first and confirm your new tests fail on it; a test that passes both ways is worth nothing here, which is exactly the trap BAD-090's reviewer caught.

Spawn ONE reviewer as your child (persona reviewer, model opus) before you return, and give it the diff, this brief and BAD-090's outcome. BAD-090's first cut was blocked by its reviewer for this precise class of mistake — a supersession guard wrapping a transfer — so the review is the part of this ticket most likely to earn its cost. Wait for it inside your turn and act on what it says.

Two findings that shape the fix: (1) the only callers that pass pull:true are web/collabweb-model.js:251 onSceneSelected and renderer/app.js:1688 selectPack — autoPullWrapped goes through runCollabSync on BOTH clients already (web/collabweb-sync.js:285, renderer/app.js:6133), so post-BAD-090 it is NOT under the refresh's guard and the brief's 'autoPullWrapped is worse' is stale; (2) the snapshot handoff differs per client — web's pullTakes reads collab.info (written BELOW the guard today), desktop's collab:pull reads main's collabInfoSnaps, which absorbCollabInfo fills inside the collab:status handler with no renderer seq near it. So the web needs the snapshot write moved above the guard (monotonic, so a late read never replaces a newer one) and the desktop does not.
